data.title: Antimony Resources Corp. (ATMY) (ATMYF) (K8J0) Announces Closing of Order Book for Financing
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 16, 2026) - Antimony Resources Corp. (OTCQB: ATMYF) (FSE: K8J0) (the "Company" or "ATMY") is pleased to announce the Company has closed its order book of the non-brokered private placement financing under the Listed Issuer Financing Exemption (as defined below), whereby the Company intends to raise up to $3,000,000 through an offering of up to 10,000,000 units of the Company (the "Units") to be priced at $0.30 per Unit (the "Offering"). The securities offered under the Listed Issuer Financing Exemption will not be subject to a hold period in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws.

The Offering has been fully subscribed with one strategic mining investor.

Each Unit will consist of one common share in the capital of the Company (each, a "Common Share") and one-half of one Common Share purchase warrant (each whole warrant, a "Warrant"). Each Warrant will entitle the holder thereof to purchase one Common Share of the Company at an exercise price of $0.50 per Common Share for a period of two years following the completion of the Offering.

The Company intends to use the net proceeds of the Offering to fund exploration and development activities on its Bald Hill Antimony Project, as well as for general working capital purposes. Finder's fees may be payable in accordance with the policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange.

The Offering is scheduled to close on or about October 21, 2026, and is subject to certain conditions including, but not limited to, the receipt of all necessary approvals. Subject to compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and in accordance with National Instrument 45-106 - Prospectus Exemptions ("NI 45-106"), the Offering is being made to purchasers resident in Canada, except Quebec, pursuant to the listed issuer financing exemption under Part 5A of NI 45-106 (the "Listed Issuer Financing Exemption"). The securities offered under the Listed Issuer Financing Exemption will not be subject to a hold period in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws.

There is an offering document related to this Offering that can be accessed under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the Company's website at https://antimonyresources.ca/. Prospective investors should read this offering document before making an investment decision.

Bald Hill Antimony Project - A Project with Significant Antimony Potential

Highlights

  • Bald Hill is a well-known, high-grade antimony deposit in southern New Brunswick, Canada.
  • Assays indicate that Bald Hill is the highest-grade antimony deposit in North America with mineable grades and widths indicated by drilling.
  • Drilling has outlined an antimony deposit in the Main Zone over 600 meters long and to a depth of at least 350 meters. The mineralization is open in all directions.
  • Widths of mineralization average 4 to 5 meters and grades average 3% to 4% antimony.
  • NI-43-101 Technical Report: The estimated potential quantity and grade of the drilled area from the 2025 Technical Report, which is the target of our exploration, is reported in the Technical Reports approximately 2.7 million tonnes with a grade between 3% and 4% antimony1. For more details on the Potential of the project as described by the author of the Technical Report please consult the NI43-101 which has been filed on SEDAR. Antimony Resources Corp. has not completed enough work to confirm this estimate. The potential quantity and grade are conceptual in nature as there has been insufficient exploration to define a mineral resource, and it is uncertain if further exploration will result in the target being delineated as a mineral resource.
  • Potential to expand based on recently discovered targets and additional claims added to the property to the west, south and east.
  • New Zones outlined by Soil Sampling approximately 3 kilometres south of the Main Zone on the newly acquired Second Run Claim.

(1) NATIONAL INSTRUMENT 43-101 TECHNICAL REPORT: BALD HILL ANTIMONY PROJECT, SOUTHERN NEW BRUNSWICK, CANADA, NTS 21G/09 Prepared for Antimony Resources March 2, 2026. Prepared By John Langton, M.Sc., P. GEO., JPL GeoServices, Fredericton, New Brunswick, Canada.

The technical contents of this news release were reviewed and approved by Jim Atkinson, MSc., P. Geo., President and CEO of Antimony Resources Corp. who is a qualified person as defined by National Instrument 43-101.

Antimony Resources Corp. is an exploration and development company focused exclusively on Antimony. The Company's management team possesses extensive experience in financing, exploration, development and mining. The Company is focused on becoming a significant North American producer of antimony.

data.title: Sandpiper comes out against H&R's proposed Go REIT deal
data.description:
Sandpiper Group, which owns about 1% of outstanding H&R Real Estate Investment Trust (HR.UN:CA) (), is against H&R's planned Go Residential REIT (GO.U:CA) (GO.U) deal.

"The central question is whether this particular transaction delivers compelling value to H&R's public unitholders on terms that are transparent, balanced, and in our best interests. We have serious concerns that it does not," said Samir Manji, founder and CEO of Sandpiper Group, in a statement on Friday. "That is why Sandpiper intends to vote AGAINST the Transaction."

Sandpiper joins a chorus of other investors who have come out against the deal, including RBC Global Asset Management and  Mill Pond last week.

In August, H&R REIT agreed to be acquired by Go Residential and a consortium including Blackstone (), Crestpoint, PSP Investments, and a company controlled by members of the family of H&R CEO Tom Hofstedter in a deal valued at ~C$6.7B.

data.title: Understanding the New Concerns in the AI Trade — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Levine

The B-word is on everyone's lips: Are we in a bubble? As there have been in recent months, there were all kinds of signs this past week that investors are becoming less enthusiastic about the generational investments into artificial-intelligence data centers. And while the AI bubble doesn't look ready to pop yet, 2027 is shaping up as a make-or-break year for the sector.

CoreWeave, which invented the "neocloud" business model — speed running to becoming a hyperscaler — has become an AI battleground stock, especially this past week. The company is built on a cycle of debt, capex, and very rapid sales growth, with a foundation of a nearly $130 billion backlog. It's a tightrope walk across a canyon. If it keeps moving forward, there's a pot of gold on the other side, but if it stops for a second, it could all come crashing down.

Since the market close on Oct. 6, the PHLX Semiconductor index has been down seven days in a row, falling 12% all told. CoreWeave has seen its stock decline by 24% in that period. Its publicly held debt has sold off, trading at roughly 82 cents on the dollar for its 2032 senior notes. The yield to maturity is 14.4%, up from 9.6% at offering in June.

In another blow to sentiment, last week there was a kerfuffle over AI-model leader OpenAI's revenue, which was either at a $70 billion annual run rate in September or $50 billion, depending on whether gross or net sales were used for the calculation. Then, this week, Anthropic released quarterly numbers at a private investor day that failed to quell the market's concerns.

OpenAI had already decided to postpone its initial public offering while it works out the security issues that its new models are causing. It isn't alone: Australian AI cloud provider Firmus decided to delay its IPO after investors balked at the proposed $30 billion valuation, up from $11 billion in August. Anthropic, however, despite facing security issues of its own, is charging ahead with a fall offering.

But it's OpenAI's long-term commitments of over a trillion dollars — including large cloud contracts with Oracle, Microsoft, CoreWeave, and Cerebras — that remain central to everyone's worries. Many wonder if it can earn enough revenue to pay those bills, which only grow over the next five years. The bigger risk for OpenAI isn't the AI investment boom rolling over, but rather cheaper competition eating into its gross profit.

And rising long-term interest rates are a developing issue for the cloud business, which is very dependent on debt.

Investor sentiment took a downturn in September. But back on the ground, it's still full steam ahead. My No. 1 indicator is graphics processing unit rental prices, and according to data from Silicon Data and Ornn, they have been rising all year. CoreWeave has even rented out its Nvidia A100 GPUs, first released in 2020, through 2029. Even as the so-called hyperscalers add hundreds of billions of dollars worth of new capacity, demand growth continues to outpace supply.

This is being driven by several concurrent factors. In the first place, AI models took a big leap in capabilities this year, and they are finally ready for real business work, beginning with writing software code. The focus is around agents — software that can use AI models to accomplish a complex series of tasks from simple conversational commands. Agents use AI models at a pace that no human could possibly match, and it has led to a demand explosion.

In the U.S. Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey, carried out in September and October, only 28% of companies polled said that they would be using AI in the next six months. But that is up from 21% at the end of last year, and leaves a lot more room for growth.

Cheap Chinese models are putting pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic, and both companies have instituted price cuts in the past two months. Lower prices typically lead to more demand. Meta Platforms' new Wonder models put the company in the same category, and now there are three frontier AI labs instead of two, adding more pressure.

One reason the models are getting so much better this year is because the GPU clusters they are being built on are getting massive. Meta Wonder was trained at Meta's sprawling Prometheus data center. OpenAI's best model, Astra, was trained on 100,000 Nvidia GPUs at Oracle's Abilene, Texas, data center. These clusters will have to get larger with each generation.

The biggest near-term danger to the AI boom isn't demand; it's capital and politics. Nvidia, Broadcom, Microsoft, Cisco, and others have worked with lenders like BlackRock and Apollo Global Management to create investment vehicles totaling hundreds of billions of dollars to fund AI infrastructure. But as the price of CoreWeave debt shows, some lenders are getting more selective, while others are looking for the exit.

There is also growing local political opposition to data centers, one of the few issues that can cross party lines in the U.S. Data centers have already been canceled, delayed, or downsized, and state and local regulation may follow.

The classic sign of a bubble is concentrated investment in a single asset class, in this case AI data centers. In the past year, domestic investment into data center buildings, computers, networking equipment, software, and research accounted for nearly all the growth in U.S. fixed investment. Just five companies are spending up to $750 billion on capital expenditures this year, with likely more coming in 2028.

For the investment boom to continue, that has to change next year. Meanwhile, investors should remember that the late stages of stock market bubbles can be the most profitable. In 1999, before the implosion of the dot-com bubble the following year, the Nasdaq Composite index was up 86%, after nearly tripling over the previous four years.

Until it's your enemy, the bubble is your ally.

Write to adam.levine@barrons.com

data.title: Air Canada Expands Canada-U.S. Connectivity with New Summer 2027 Routes, Increasing Options for Travellers Under its Transborder Joint Business Agreement with United Airlines
data.description:
Key points:
  • Air Canada will launch new service from Toronto to Louisville, Montréal to Indianapolis and Edmonton to Newark; United Airlines will launch seasonal service to St. John’s from Newark and will add new service from Denver to Ottawa and to Québec City
  • New and expanded services will strengthen connectivity between Canadian communities, key U.S. destinations, and connecting hubs
  • Air Canada and United Airlines have agreed to renew and expand their Transborder Joint Business Agreement, which supports more than 1,200 connecting itineraries and continued network growth between Canada and the United States, subject to regulatory approval

MONTRÉAL, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Air Canada, together with its partner United Airlines, today announced new transborder routes for summer 2027, expanding non-stop access to U.S. destinations and providing customers with convenient connections across the United States.

Beginning next summer, Air Canada will launch new service between Toronto and Louisville, Montréal and Indianapolis, and Edmonton and Newark. Air Canada will also increase capacity between Edmonton and San Francisco by deploying the larger Airbus A220 on the route.

The new routes broaden Air Canada’s U.S. network with new links from Canadian airports to a wider range of U.S. cities. Toronto-Louisville service will begin in late April, before increasing to daily service in May. New Montréal-Indianapolis service will add another non-stop U.S. destination from Montréal, while Edmonton-Newark will provide a new direct link to the New York region and convenient connections through one of United Airlines’ global hubs.

Also beginning next summer, United is launching new seasonal service to St. John’s from its Newark hub, adding new service from Denver to Ottawa and Québec City, increasing flights between Washington, D.C., and Québec City, and increasing daily seats between Denver and Winnipeg by 65 per cent.

The new routes build on Air Canada and United’s long-standing partnership and their Transborder Joint Business Agreement. Since it was established in 2022, 20 new routes have been created between Canada and the U.S., and more than 4.3 million passengers have flown jointly on United and Air Canada. Together, Air Canada and United Airlines serve 10 Canadian gateways.

For Canadian customers, the partnership plays an important role in supporting connectivity between communities across Canada and the U.S. It brings approximately two million customers connecting to or from the U.S. onto Air Canada’s domestic network each year, providing benefits to more than 50 communities across Canada and strengthening the overall sustainability and connectivity of our domestic services. Beyond our main hubs, the partnership enables direct transborder services from Calgary, Edmonton, Halifax, Ottawa, Québec City, Regina, St. John’s and Winnipeg.

Customers also have access to more than 1,200 connecting itineraries, with integrated through-fares that can offer meaningful savings compared with purchasing individual flight segments separately. Coordinated schedules also provide more departure options, improved connections and greater flexibility during disruptions, helping make the respective networks more resilient and better able to serve customers when travel is disrupted.

Building on these benefits, Air Canada and United Airlines have agreed to renew and expand their Transborder Joint Business Agreement, subject to the necessary regulatory approvals. An application has been submitted to Transport Canada seeking approval of the amended and restated agreement.

“Air Canada and United's long-standing partnership continues to deliver meaningful results for our customers and communities. For nearly three decades, Air Canada and United have worked to facilitate seamless travel and strengthen connectivity between Canada and the United States. Together, since 2022, we have jointly unlocked over 5 million new transborder seats, and in this spirit, Air Canada will soon add new non-stop travel options from Toronto, Montréal and Edmonton for our customers to reach a broader range of global markets,” said Mark Galardo, Executive Vice President & Chief Commercial Officer, and President, Cargo at Air Canada. “From Louisville and Indianapolis to Newark, we are giving customers more ways to travel directly to U.S. destinations, together with convenient connections across United’s extensive U.S. network.”

“Canada is an incredibly important part of United’s international network, and our partnership with Air Canada has made it easier for families and friends to stay connected, supported economic growth, and created new opportunities to explore unique destinations. Our schedule has grown every year since our transborder agreement was signed in 2022, and the new routes and flights we’re announcing today further underscore our commitment to investing in Canada and making travel between our two countries easier,” said United’s Senior Vice President of Global Network Planning and Alliances, Patrick Quayle.

Air Canada and United Airlines have worked together since 1996 and are long-standing Star Alliance partners and founding members. Their relationship has evolved over nearly three decades to provide customers with more travel options, seamless connections, and reciprocal loyalty benefits between Canada and the United States.

Comments from Stakeholders

"Air Canada's investment in new non-stop service between Edmonton and New York City, via Newark Liberty International Airport, is a significant win for our region. This route opens the door to one of the world's most important business, financial and cultural centres, creating new opportunities for tourism and trade while making it easier for people and businesses to connect. We're thankful for Air Canada's continued commitment to YEG and to the people, businesses and communities we serve," said James Jackson, Vice President, Air Service and Business Development, Edmonton International Airport (YEG).

“ADM Aéroports de Montréal is pleased to announce the addition of this route to Indianapolis, offered by our partner Air Canada. This new route to one of the major economic hubs of the U.S. Midwest will make travel easier for both business travellers and tourists. The addition of Indianapolis allows YUL to enhance its travel routes to strategic destinations throughout North America,” said Karl Brochu, ADM’s Vice President, Airport Operations and Air Services Development.

"Today's announcements are a game changer for Québec City. A new direct link to Denver, year-round service to Chicago, and five weekly flights to Washington Dulles are exactly the kind of connections our tourism industry and business community need to thrive. Results like these are a direct reflection of the strength of the partnership between Air Canada and United Airlines, and of the confidence both carriers have in our market. We are proud to see that commitment translate into real, tangible benefits for our region," said Stéphane Poirier, President and CEO of Québec City Jean Lesage International Airport (YQB).

“We are thrilled with United Airlines’ announcement to re-connect YYT and Newark for the first time in more than a decade,” said Dennis Hogan, Chief Executive Officer, St. John’s International Airport. “Re-establishing non-stop service to the eastern U.S. seaboard is a strategic priority for our airport and represents a significant air access milestone. This route, made possible through the Transborder Joint Business Agreement between Air Canada and United Airlines, will enhance both business and leisure travel and unlock an extensive onward network of travel options.”

“The renewal of the Transborder Joint Business Agreement between Air Canada and United Airlines, together with a 65 per cent increase in Denver service, will provide Manitobans with greater choice, improved connectivity and added convenience when travelling,” said Nick Hays, President and CEO, Winnipeg Airports Authority.

“United Airlines’ decision to launch non-stop service between Ottawa and Denver marks an exciting expansion of their presence at YOW,” said Joel Tkach, Vice President of Business Development and Marketing for the Ottawa International Airport Authority. “Denver becomes United’s fourth destination from Canada’s Capital, further strengthening their role as Air Canada’s partner and as a key contributor to our U.S. connectivity. This new route enhances options for travellers and reinforces United’s importance in linking Ottawa–Gatineau to major hubs across the United States.”

The Transborder Joint Business Agreement at a Glance:

  • A long-standing Canada-U.S. airline partnership, connecting Air Canada and United Airlines networks to offer customers more destinations, more frequencies and more travel options than either airline could provide on its own.
  • Twenty new transborder routes enabled since launch, including six added in 2026, connecting more communities across Canada and the United States.
  • Expanded customer choice and connectivity, with transborder seat capacity growing approximately 31 per cent in 2023 and a further 7 per cent in 2024.
  • More than 1,200 integrated Canada-U.S. itineraries provide seamless single-ticket travel and economic efficiency, with customers paying significantly less on average than if they booked each flight segment separately.
  • Strengthens Canada's role as a North American gateway, connecting Canadian communities to destinations across the United States and around the world through stronger Canadian hubs.
  • Supports Canadian jobs and economic growth by strengthening trade, investment and business connectivity between Canada and the United States, and by promoting inbound tourism via championing Canadian destinations.
  • Creates a smoother travel experience, providing customers with more flight options, integrated rebooking during disruptions and greater flexibility when travel plans change.
  • Provides more convenient schedules throughout the day, including near-hourly service on key Canada-U.S. routes, offering customers greater flexibility and more departure options.
  • Maximizes utilization of constrained airport infrastructure through coordinated schedules, allowing a broader spread of departures throughout the day.
  • Strengthens Air Canada's domestic network, helping sustain connectivity through Canadian hubs and providing communities across Canada with greater access to destinations in the United States and beyond.
  • Helps sustain and grow service for smaller and regional communities, supporting routes and travel options that would be difficult for either airline to provide independently.
  • Preserves the benefits Canadians rely on today, including through-fare savings, more travel choices, expanded connectivity, stronger Canadian hubs and continued investment in communities across the country.

About Air Canada

Air Canada is Canada's largest airline, the country’s flag carrier and a founding member of Star Alliance, the world's most comprehensive air transportation network. Headquartered in Montréal, Air Canada provides scheduled service directly to more than 180 airports in Canada, the United States and internationally on six continents. It holds a Four-Star ranking from Skytrax. Air Canada’s Aeroplan program is Canada’s premier travel loyalty program, with more than 10 million members worldwide. Members can earn or redeem points on the world’s largest airline partner network of more than 50 airlines, plus through an extensive range of merchandise, hotel and car rental partners. Through Air Canada Vacations, it offers a selection of vacation and Flight & Hotel packages, tours, cruises, car rentals, and experiences. Its freight division, Air Canada Cargo, provides air freight lift and connectivity to hundreds of destinations across six continents using Air Canada’s passenger and freighter aircraft. Air Canada’s climate-related ambition includes a long-term aspirational goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. For additional information, please see Air Canada’s TCFD disclosure. Air Canada shares are publicly traded on the TSX (AC).

data.title: Snabbit's expansion push comes at a cost as FY26 losses hit Rs.168 crore
data.description:
BENGALURU, Oct. 16 -- Snabbit's losses widened nearly 30-fold to Rs.167.75 crore in fiscal year 2026 (FY26) as the instant home-help startup spent heavily on workers and marketing to build its business, highlighting the cost of scaling a service that must keep professionals close to customers to make each booking viable.

Revenue from operations rose to Rs.12.25 crore in the year ended 31 March 2026 from Rs.26.35 lakh a year earlier, while expenses surged to Rs.194.76 crore from Rs.6.81 crore, according to financial statements of Maestroedge Solutions Pvt. Ltd, which operates Snabbit. The company had reported a loss of Rs.5.70 crore in FY25.

Costs relating to professionals were Snabbit's largest expense at Rs.63.07 crore, followed by marketing at Rs.48.69 crore, employee expenses at Rs.46.02 crore and service fulfilment expenses at Rs.23.83 crore.

Revenue included Rs.10.82 crore from platform services and Rs.1.42 crore from uniform sales. Snabbit reports revenue after deducting discounts it pays for to lower customers' bills.

Other income, mainly interest on bank deposits, contributed Rs.14.77 crore, taking total income to Rs.27.01 crore.

The spending reflects a familiar challenge from food delivery's early years, when platforms funded discounts and delivery costs to attract customers. Instant-help companies face a similar task: persuading households to try a new service while ensuring enough workers are available to fulfil bookings.

Snabbit raised $56 million in April, taking its total funding to more than $112 million across five rounds. Its valuation in that round was reported at $350-400 million. Rival Pronto has raised about $60 million and was valued at $200 million in its latest round.

Urban Company's board approved plans on Friday to raise up to Rs.2,500 crore, subject to shareholder approval. The company said the proposed fundraising would support its established businesses, InstaHelp and potential acquisitions.

The bigger challenge is making the economics work beyond densely packed neighbourhoods.

Mint reported in August that instant-help providers such as Snabbit, Pronto, and Urban Company's InstaHelp may have to nearly double prices as they expand into areas where homes are farther apart and workers have fewer bookings.

Currently, each professional completes 8-10 jobs over about 9.5 working hours a day, keeping the total servicing cost at Rs.95-100 an hour, according to industry estimates cited in the report. This is also close to what customers pay in many cases.

That cost structure depends on jobs being clustered within a 300-400-metre walking radius. Longer journeys leave workers with less time to complete paid bookings, increasing the cost of each job.

Experts said prices may eventually need to rise above Rs.200 an hour to make the model profitable. For now, platforms are focusing on high-demand neighbourhoods, assigning workers nearby jobs in succession and charging more during peak hours.

Snabbit used Rs.157.46 crore in operating activities in FY26, equivalent to an average monthly cash burn of Rs.13.12 crore. The full-year average, however, may not reflect its spending rate in FY27.

The company ended FY26 with Rs.292.21 crore in cash and bank balances, including Rs.285.70 crore in deposits, and another Rs.26.65 crore in mutual funds. These balances predate its April funding round.

data.title: RBI approves Emirates NBD merger with RBL Bank from December 1: 5 key things to know
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved the amalgamation of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C.'s Indian branches with RBL Bank Ltd, with the merger set to take effect from 1 December 2026. From that date, all Indian branches of Emirates NBD will function as branches of RBL Bank, according to RBI's announcement on 16 October.

The approval marks a key step in Emirates NBD's expansion in India following its acquisition of a majority stake in RBL Bank in June 2026. Here are five key things to know about the merger.

RBI has sanctioned the scheme of amalgamation of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C.'s Indian branches, referred to as the transferor bank, with RBL Bank Ltd, the transferee bank.

The approval was granted under Section 44A(4) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. RBI has specified 1 December 2026 as the effective date of the amalgamation.

The decision clears the way for Emirates NBD's Indian branch operations to be consolidated under RBL Bank. The amalgamation is part of the broader transaction announced by the two banks in October 2025.

Emirates NBD completed its acquisition of a majority stake in RBL Bank on 18 June 2026 through a primary capital infusion of approximately $2.75 billion, or Rs.26,000 crore. The investment gave the UAE-based banking group a 60% stake in RBL Bank's expanded share capital.

The transaction was first announced on 18 October 2025. Under the agreement, Emirates NBD subscribed to newly issued RBL Bank shares through a preferential allotment. The deal was completed after the required regulatory approvals and closing conditions were satisfied.

The acquisition and branch amalgamation are separate stages of the transaction. While the investment was completed in June, the merger of Emirates NBD's Indian branches will take effect in December.

Emirates NBD operates in India through three branches located in Mumbai, Chennai and Gurugram. The Competition Commission of India (CCI), in its announcement dated 20 January 2026, confirmed that the proposed combination included the amalgamation of these branches with RBL Bank on a going-concern basis.

RBI's latest approval confirms that all Indian branches of Emirates NBD will function as RBL Bank branches from 1 December.

The arrangement will bring Emirates NBD's Indian branch operations under RBL Bank, an Indian-incorporated and listed private sector lender. Emirates NBD will remain the controlling shareholder following the acquisition of its majority stake.

Emirates NBD and RBL Bank described the transaction as the largest foreign direct investment in the Indian banking sector and the largest equity fundraise in the sector. They also said it marked the first acquisition of a majority interest in a profitable Indian bank by a foreign bank.

The investment provides RBL Bank with additional capital to support its growth plans, while giving Emirates NBD a controlling presence in India. The banks said the transaction would bring together Emirates NBD's regional banking expertise and network with RBL Bank's established domestic franchise.

The CCI approved the proposed combination on 20 January 2026. Its announcement covered Emirates NBD's proposed acquisition of a stake of between 51% and 74% in RBL Bank through a preferential allotment and mandatory open offer, along with the amalgamation of Emirates NBD's Indian banking operations with RBL Bank.

On 15 May 2026, RBL Bank announced that it had received the required regulatory and governmental approvals for the investment. The acquisition was subsequently completed in June.

RBI's approval on 16 October is the latest milestone in the process, setting 1 December 2026 as the effective date for the branch amalgamation.

data.title: NSE Anchor Book Shows Growing Clout Of Domestic Institutional Capital
data.description:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s Rs 6,746 crore anchor book has highlighted the growing influence of domestic institutions in India’s primary market, with local investors accounting for more than half of total anchor mobilisation.

Domestic anchors contributed around Rs 3,464 crore, or 51.4 per cent of the overall anchor book, putting them marginally ahead of international investors. The numbers also point to the increasing ability of Indian merchant bankers to mobilise large pools of institutional capital, narrowing the gap with global investment banks in major domestic transactions.

Indian Merchant Bankers Nearly Match Global Peers

Five domestic merchant bankers — Kotak Mahindra Capital, SBICAPS, JM Financial, Axis Capital and Pantomath Capital — collectively mobilised Rs 3,261 crore, representing about 48.3 per cent of the Rs 6,746 crore anchor book. Their combined mobilisation was close to the Rs 3,282 crore brought in by four major international banks — Morgan Stanley, Citi, HSBC and JP Morgan.

The domestic group includes established investment banking franchises alongside Pantomath Capital, reflecting the widening base of institutions participating in large primary-market transactions. While international banks continue to provide access to overseas long-only funds, sovereign wealth funds and other global institutions, Indian merchant bankers have developed access to a growing pool of domestic mutual funds, insurers, pension funds and other institutional investors.

Mutual Funds Take 37% Of Allocation

Domestic mutual funds received nearly 37 per cent of the anchor allocation, while foreign portfolio investors accounted for around 43 per cent. Life Insurance Corporation of India emerged as the largest individual anchor investor. International institutions participating in the transaction included Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global, the Monetary Authority of Singapore and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.

The composition indicates that India's primary market is increasingly being supported by two sizeable sources of institutional capital — global investors accessed through international banks and a deepening domestic investor base mobilised by Indian institutions. The anchor book also reflects the broader expansion of India's domestic capital-market infrastructure, with local institutional investors playing a larger role in supporting major equity offerings.

The NSE IPO subscription process continued on September 19, with the issue subscribed 1.16 times by the end of the second day, according to exchange data.

data.title: Radico Khaitan Elevates Sakshi Arora To Joint General Manager
data.description:
Arora will lead Rampur Indian Single Malt Whisky globally after a double promotion

Radico Khaitan has promoted Sakshi Arora to Joint General Manager (JGM), marking a double promotion in her career at the spirits maker. In her new role, Arora will lead Rampur Indian Single Malt Whisky globally.

Arora shared the development on LinkedIn, describing 2026 as a significant year in her professional journey and expressing gratitude to Sanjeev Banga and Kunal Madan for their trust and support.

She previously served as Associate General Manager (AGM) – Global Brand Head, Rampur Indian Single Malt, from October 2024 to October 2026. During this period, she led the brand’s marketing across India and more than 30 international markets, including the UK, the US, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, as well as Global Travel Retail. She managed an annual marketing investment of approximately Rs 45 crore and worked on portfolio development, global brand strategy and integrated marketing initiatives.

Arora joined Radico Khaitan in June 2019 as Senior Manager – Marketing, handling Rampur Indian Single Malt and Jaisalmer Indian Craft Gin across domestic and international markets. Over the years, she has worked on global product launches, premium brand development and partnerships, including Rampur’s Michelin association and its Jugalbandi Series, which received a Best Travel Retail Award.

Before joining Radico Khaitan, Arora held marketing roles at Rohto Pharmaceutical, RAL Consumer Products and DS Group.

data.title: Ajay Kumar Ojha takes charge as F&B manager at Holiday Inn Gurugram Sector 90
data.description:
Holiday Inn Gurugram Sector 90 has appointed Ajay Kumar Ojha as food and beverage manager. He brings more than 15 years of hospitality experience across food and beverage operations, banqueting and team leadership.

Ojha has held roles with ITC Hotels, Marriott Hotels & Resorts, The LaLiT, Jaypee Hotels and IHG. His experience includes an earlier association with Crowne Plaza Jaipur, where he was part of the pre-opening team. His appointment marks his return to IHG.

Before joining Holiday Inn Gurugram Sector 90, Ojha served as F&B manager at ITC Fortune Select Global, Gurugram, overseeing multiple outlets, banqueting, room service, inventory management, food safety, cost control and revenue generation.

He is also a certified trainer and holds certifications from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) and the Food Safety Training and Certification (FoSTaC) programme.

In his new role, Ojha will lead the hotel’s food and beverage operations, focussing on guest experience, team development, revenue performance and adherence to IHG brand standards.

Rishabh Jain, general manager, Holiday Inn Gurugram Sector 90, said, “It is an absolute pleasure to welcome Ajay back to the IHG family and to Holiday Inn Gurugram Sector 90. As we continue to strengthen our food and beverage offerings, Ajay’s expertise will play an important role in elevating guest experiences, developing our teams and driving sustainable commercial performance. We look forward to his contribution as we continue to build a distinctive and compelling F&B proposition for our guests."

data.title: Vikram Solar Adds 187 MW Module Order Across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu
data.description:
The contract covers high-efficiency solar modules for projects across three locations, adding to the company’s domestic order pipeline

Vikram Solar has secured a 187 MW solar module supply order from an undisclosed renewable energy developer for projects across Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The order covers N-Type Tunnel Oxide Passivated Contact (TOPCon) G12R modules with power ratings ranging from 615 watts-peak (Wp) to 625 Wp.

The modules feature bifacial technology and glass-to-glass construction. The company has not disclosed the contract value, delivery schedule, or capacity allocation across the three project locations.

Focus On Module Technology

The modules use bifacial technology, which allows them to generate electricity from sunlight captured on both sides of the panel. Actual generation gains depend on installation design and site conditions.

The glass-to-glass construction uses glass on both sides of the module, while the TOPCon cell architecture supports high-efficiency power generation. These specifications form part of the equipment offering for utility-scale solar projects.

Strengthening The Order Book

The contract adds to Vikram Solar’s domestic order pipeline as demand for solar equipment supports India’s renewable energy expansion. Module supply agreements provide manufacturers with visibility into demand from project developers, although the financial contribution of an individual order depends on its value and execution schedule.

Sameer Nagpal, Chief Executive Officer of Vikram Solar, said the expansion of the solar sector has increased the focus on technology, reliability, and long-term performance in utility-scale projects, and the company would continue to develop its technology capabilities and maintain its manufacturing and execution standards to meet customer requirements.

data.title: Tata Power Seeks Bengal Solar Incentives, Plans Rs 2,500 Cr Investment
data.description:
Land availability and high upfront installation costs remain key hurdles as the company explores 500 MW of solar projects in West Bengal

Tata Power has urged the West Bengal government to offer additional subsidies for rooftop solar installations as the company explores an investment of around Rs 2,500 crore in solar projects across the state. The proposals aim to improve household access to solar energy and expand renewable power generation, although both affordability and land availability remain key challenges.

The company has proposed additional state incentives under the Centre’s PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, particularly for low-income households. Separately, Tata Power is assessing solar projects with a combined capacity of around 500 MW. The investment remains at an early stage, with project locations and capacity allocations yet to be finalised.

The Cost Of Going Solar

The Centre provides a subsidy of Rs 30,000 for a 1 kW rooftop solar installation and up to Rs 78,000 for a 3 kW system. Tata Power believes additional state support could make installations more affordable for households that struggle to meet the upfront cost.

Sanjay Banga, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Tata Power Renewable Energy Ltd, has urged West Bengal to consider incentives similar to those offered by Odisha, Bihar and Assam. According to the company, these states provide additional support of Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per project, as per a media report.

Tata Power has installed around 6,000 rooftop solar systems in West Bengal out of nearly 22,000 households covered under the programme in the state, according to company data.

Financing is another part of the challenge. Tata Power has introduced a zero-down-payment residential solar scheme in partnership with banks to reduce the initial financial burden on customers. Additional state subsidies could complement such financing arrangements and improve affordability.

Rs 2,500 Crore Solar Plan

Alongside its rooftop solar push, Tata Power is exploring multiple solar power projects across West Bengal with a combined capacity of around 500 MW and a potential investment of Rs 2,500 crore.

The state government has offered three to four locations for assessment. Tata Power will evaluate their viability before deciding where to develop projects and how to distribute the proposed capacity. The company may spread the projects across multiple sites rather than establish one large solar facility.

Land availability remains a key constraint. The proposed investment will depend on the suitability of the identified sites and the commercial viability of the projects.

Solar Parks To Cut Costs

Tata Power has proposed that West Bengal identify non-agricultural land for solar parks, develop the necessary infrastructure and invite private companies to establish projects.

Under this model, the state would facilitate the development of solar parks, while private companies would install generation facilities and supply electricity to the West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Ltd (WBSEDCL) under long-term power purchase agreements.

Banga has estimated that electricity from such projects could cost around Rs 3 per unit, compared with WBSEDCL’s average power procurement cost of Rs 4-5 per unit. The final cost would depend on project economics and the terms of the power purchase agreements, as per a media report.

Tata Power has cited approaches adopted by Rajasthan and Karnataka as examples of state-led efforts to facilitate solar project development. The proposed model would require West Bengal to identify suitable land and provide the infrastructure needed to make projects commercially viable.

The company’s proposals address two separate challenges in the state’s solar expansion: the upfront cost of rooftop installations for households and the availability of land for larger renewable energy projects. Progress will depend on the state government’s response to the subsidy proposal and the viability of the sites under consideration.

data.title: Urban Company’s Q2 Loss Widens To Rs 182 Cr, InstaHelp Spending Rises
data.description:
Urban Company’s revenue rises 41.3 per cent to Rs 537.3 crore in Q2FY27, while losses from its instant household-help service InstaHelp widen to Rs 173.12 crore

Urban Company’s net loss widened more than threefold year-on-year in the second quarter of FY27 as rising expenditure on its instant household-help service, InstaHelp, offset strong revenue growth. The home services platform reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 182 crore, compared with Rs 59 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Revenue rose 41.3 per cent year-on-year to Rs 537.3 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 380 crore a year earlier. However, the company’s Ebitda loss also increased to Rs 188 crore from Rs 68.7 crore, reflecting the cost of expanding its operations.

InstaHelp Drives Losses

Urban Company’s segment performance showed contrasting trends across its businesses. India consumer services, excluding InstaHelp, reported revenue of Rs 336.38 crore and segment profit of Rs 43.39 crore, up from Rs 10.13 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Revenue from its international business increased to Rs 75 crore from Rs 41.19 crore, while segment profit rose to Rs 5.74 crore. Native, the company’s home-products business, recorded revenue of Rs 105.37 crore but reported a segment loss of Rs 7.95 crore.

InstaHelp remained the biggest contributor to the company’s losses. The service generated revenue of Rs 20.54 crore, while its segment loss widened to Rs 173.12 crore from Rs 42.91 crore in Q2FY26.

The widening loss reflects the investment required to scale on-demand household help, a segment in which Urban Company competes with platforms such as Snabbit and Pronto.

Urban Company Considers Rs 2,500 Cr Fundraise

Urban Company is considering raising up to Rs 2,500 crore through equity, debt and other financing routes to support its business plans. The proposed fundraising comes as the company continues to invest in InstaHelp and evaluates opportunities for further expansion.

The company is also exploring residential air conditioners as a potential new business line, which could broaden its presence in the home-products market beyond its existing services and product offerings.

Urban Company’s immediate challenge is to sustain revenue growth while managing the cost of expansion. Its India consumer services business, excluding InstaHelp, and international operations are profitable at the segment level, but losses from the instant household-help service continue to weigh heavily on overall financial performance.

data.title: Suraj Singh Set To Join Zee Studios
data.description:
He is currently the Co-founder of Blive Productions & Music

Suraj Singh, Co-founder of Blive Productions & Music, is set to join Zee Studios, bringing over two decades of experience across film and television production.

The proposed appointment comes amid changes in the studio’s senior leadership. Umesh Bansal stepped down from Zee Studios to take charge as Managing Director and CEO at B4U/IVY. Pragati Deshmukh, who was appointed Head of Content across verticals at Zee Studios in June 2024, has also moved on and is now a producer at Spellbound Labs.

Zee Studios’ Hindi film team also includes Raedita Tandan, who was appointed Co-Producer – Hindi Films in April 2026 after joining the studio as Creative Producer in September 2025. Tandan has previously worked with Junglee Pictures, Luv Films and Abundantia Entertainment, with experience spanning creative development, film and series production, marketing and communications. Before entering the production business, she held editorial roles at entertainment publications, including Filmfare.

Before co-founding Blive Productions & Music, Singh held senior positions at Balaji Telefilms, including Vice President and Vice President of Television Production & Operations. His responsibilities included overseeing production, coordinating with broadcasters on budgets and creative requirements, and securing new programming mandates.

During his tenure at Balaji Telefilms, he worked on projects including The Dirty Picture, Kyaa Super Kool Hain Hum, Ek Thi Daayan, Shootout at Wadala, Lootera, Ragini MMS 2 and Ek Villain.

His television experience includes a stint as Creative Producer at Sphere Origins Multivision, where he worked on storylines, screenplays and casting, while coordinating with broadcasters.

Singh is the brother of Prerna Singh, who has served as Chief Executive Officer of Bhansali Productions.

data.title: Aster CMI Hospital Performs India’s First Reported Pediatric Kidney Swap Transplant
data.description:
Two-way donor exchange enables a 15-year-old boy and a 21-year-old man to receive compatible kidneys despite blood group mismatch

Aster CMI Hospital, Bengaluru, has successfully performed what it describes as India’s first reported pediatric ABO-incompatible kidney transplant through a two-way donor swap, enabling a 15-year-old boy and a 21-year-old man to undergo kidney transplantation despite blood group incompatibility with their intended family donors.

The procedure used Alliance for Paired Donation (APD) software to identify compatible donor-recipient combinations. Both patients had relatives willing to donate, but direct transplantation was not feasible because of blood group mismatch. Through kidney-paired donation, the donors exchanged recipients, allowing each patient to receive a kidney from the other family.

Kidney-paired donation is designed to address incompatibilities involving blood groups and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) matching in living-donor transplantation. In this case, the teenager received a kidney from the 21-year-old patient’s family donor, while the latter received a kidney from the teenager’s family donor.

Months Of Planning

The complex transplant required months of logistical planning and coordination, with four operating theatres functioning simultaneously. The procedures involved four anaesthetists and four transplant surgical teams, along with support from infectious disease specialists and other multidisciplinary teams.

According to Aster CMI Hospital, technology-enabled matching allowed multiple donor-recipient combinations to be assessed simultaneously to identify suitable exchange opportunities. The hospital said the approach could reduce the likelihood of requiring repeat transplantation and may lower post-transplant infection risks. It also estimated that the method could reduce costs by about 40% compared with conventional approaches.

Dr Arun Kumar N, Senior Consultant – Nephrology and Renal Transplant, Aster CMI Hospital, said the technology helped identify appropriate matches while coordinated multidisciplinary efforts enabled the simultaneous procedures.

Dr Avinash T S, Lead Consultant – Urology, Aster CMI Hospital, said paired donation provided a pathway for transplantation when direct donation was not possible because of blood group incompatibility. He highlighted the importance of compatible matching, meticulous planning and simultaneous surgical coordination.

Sudhindra G Bhat, Chief Operating Officer, Aster DM Quality Care, said paired donation could create new possibilities for families unable to proceed with direct transplantation. Dr Prashant N, Regional Chief Executive Officer, Aster DM Quality Care, said technology-driven donor matching could help expand the living-donor pool for patients facing donor incompatibility.

data.title: Oberoi Realty Q2 Revenue Falls 6% To Rs 1,671 Cr, Profit Holds Steady
data.description:
The real estate developer reported consolidated net profit of Rs 761.65 crore for the September quarter, while revenue from operations declined to Rs 1,670.95 crore

Oberoi Realty reported a marginal 0.2 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 761.65 crore for the second quarter of FY27, while revenue from operations fell 6.1 per cent to Rs 1,670.95 crore. The company had reported a net profit of Rs 760.26 crore and revenue from operations of Rs 1,779.04 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Total income for the quarter declined to Rs 1,736.37 crore from Rs 1,844.80 crore a year earlier. Finance costs fell to Rs 58.14 crore from Rs 71.2 crore, while the operating margin increased to 60.99 per cent from 57.35 per cent. Revenue from the real estate segment stood at Rs 1,625.34 crore, compared with Rs 1,734.4 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue from the hospitality segment edged up to Rs 45.61 crore from Rs 44.6 crore.

For the six months ended 30 September, Oberoi Realty’s consolidated net profit increased 10.5 per cent to Rs 1,305.16 crore from Rs 1,181.51 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 2,971.8 crore from Rs 2,766.6 crore. On a standalone basis, net profit increased 19.1 per cent to Rs 735.88 crore from Rs 618.02 crore. Total standalone revenue, including other income, stood at Rs 1,588.1 crore, compared with Rs 1,609.6 crore a year earlier.

The company’s consolidated debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.14 as of 30 September compared with 0.18 a year earlier. Its consolidated net worth was Rs 19,089.92 crore.

“The demand in India for real estate continues to be driven by a preference for quality, brand credibility and execution, with established developers and proven delivery track records continuing to attract sustained interest,” Vikas Oberoi, Chairman and Managing Director of Oberoi Realty, said.

He said the company’s residential, commercial, retail and hospitality businesses had delivered steady performance during the quarter, reflecting the strength of its diversified portfolio. “Our entry into NCR with our project Three Sixty North marked an important milestone in Oberoi Realty’s journey. The Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) market continues to demonstrate its depth and resilience, and we remain encouraged by demand trends as we enter the festive period,” he said.

Declares Rs 2 Interim Dividend

The board declared a second interim dividend of Rs 2 per share, equivalent to 20 per cent of the share’s face value of Rs 10. The record date and payment date should be confirmed against the company’s separate dividend disclosure before publication.

Oberoi Realty also redeemed Rs 135 crore of Series 2 non-convertible debentures. The company said its trading window would reopen on October 19.

data.title: Gasoline refining margins dip
data.description:
Northwest European gasoline refining margins fell more than $15 to their lowest since mid-June to $26.56 a barrel on Friday as oil prices jumped close to $110 a barrel .

  • In the Argus window, 9,000 metric tons of Eurobob E5 barges traded, with Equinor, Exxon and Aramco selling to TotalEnergies, Gunvor and MB Energy.

  • Shell also sold one cargo to TotalEnergies and two to Trafigura in the Platts window.

  • Shell and Exxon sold 8,000 tons of Eurobob E10 barges to Varo and BP.

  • Formosa Petrochemical, among Asia's largest fuel exporters, is reducing crude oil processing at its refinery in Mailiao, Taiwan, as it conducts maintenance at several units, the company's president said.

  • Meanwhile Asian gasoline margins nearly halved on Friday from a record high hit at the beginning of the month, as Chinese refiners resumed fuel exports, easing immediate supply concerns, traders and analysts said.​

data.title: 2027 Ducati Panigale V4 Unveiled: Gets More Power, New Tech; India Launch Next Year
data.description:
The updated superbike gets revised engine tuning, a lighter-feeling chassis setup and new electronic controls. Ducati claims a 0.4-second improvement in average lap times at Vallelunga over the previous model

Luxury motorcycle manufacturer, Ducati has unveiled the 2027 Panigale V4 with updates to its engine, chassis, aerodynamics and electronics, improving track performance and making the bike easier to control at the limit. The superbike retains its 1,103 cc Desmosedici Stradale V4 engine but now produces 218 hp, up by 2 hp over the previous model.

The updated motorcycle recorded an average lap-time improvement of 0.4 seconds at Italy's Vallelunga circuit. The new Panigale V4 is expected to arrive in India in 2027, although pricing and the launch date have not been announced.

What's New On The 2027 Panigale V4?

More power and revised gearing: Changes to the exhaust, air intake and lubrication system raise output to 218 hp. Peak torque remains rated at 120.6 Nm. Power gains are most pronounced between 12,000 and 14,000 rpm, including a claimed 3.5 hp increase at 13,000 rpm. The rev limiter now reaches 15,000 rpm in second through fifth gears, while revised final gearing (17/42, previously 16/41) is intended to reduce gear changes. Ducati reports two fewer shifts per lap at Vallelunga.

Revised chassis: The Front Frame's lateral stiffness has been reduced by 12 per cent to improve front-tyre contact and feedback at high lean angles. Ducati also says the revised final-drive setup effectively shortens the wheelbase by 8 mm, helping the bike change direction more quickly.

New braking electronics: Dynamic Engine Brake (DEB) replaces the previous Engine Brake Control, using the Ducati Vehicle Observer algorithm to adjust engine braking according to rear-tyre load. New Race Brake Control (RBC) increases the rear wheel's contribution during deceleration. Both systems are designed to improve braking stability and allow later braking and tighter corner entry.

Updated aerodynamics and ergonomics: The bike gets redesigned biplane wings with enlarged side endplates. The Panigale V4 S also gains adjustable clip-on handlebars raised by 10 mm for improved leverage and reduced rider effort during track riding. This adjustment is reserved for track use.

Factory personalisation: For the first time, the Panigale V4 S joins Ducati's Factory Made programme, which offers factory-installed colours, liveries and selected homologated components.

Ducati Panigale V4 S: Key Specifications & Features

SpecificationDetails
Engine1,103 cc Desmosedici Stradale V4
Maximum power218 hp at 13,500 rpm
Maximum torque120.6 Nm at 11,000 rpm
Rev limiter15,000 rpm in gears 2–5
Kerb weight, without fuel187 kg
Fuel tank17 litres, aluminium
ChassisFront Frame, revised lateral stiffness
Front suspensionÖhlins NPX-30 fork, Smart EC 3.0
Rear suspensionÖhlins TTX 36, Smart EC 3.0
Steering damperÖhlins Smart EC 3.0
WheelsForged aluminium
BrakesBrembo Hypure monobloc calipers
TyresPirelli Diablo Supercorsa V4; 200/60 rear
DashboardNew 6.9-inch full-TFT display, 8:3 aspect ratio
Electronics6-axis IMU, cornering Race eCBS, DTC DVO, DSC, DWC DVO, DPL DVO, DQS 2.0, DEB and RBC
Riding modesRace A, Race B, Sport, Road and Wet
LightingFull LED, with DRL and turn signals integrated into the headlight
Other featuresLithium battery, single-seat setup, Ducati Data Logger and Multimedia System pre-configuration

The S variant also features Ducati Electronic Suspension (DES) 3.0, an enlarged front air intake, revised biplane wings and buttons for quick adjustment of electronic settings.

Standard Panigale V4 vs Panigale V4 S

The standard Panigale V4 shares the S model's core engine and standard equipment, including its 218 hp output and updated electronics, but uses a different suspension and wheel package.

Optional Racing Exhaust & Customisation

Ducati will offer an Akrapovič Full Racing Exhaust PRO for track-focused use. The company claims it adds 11 hp and 7 Nm of torque while reducing weight by 6.6 kg.

Under the Ducati Factory Made programme, the Panigale V4 S can be configured with 11 colour options: Ducati Red, Ducati Yellow, Thrilling Black, GP19 Red, Aviator Grey, Arctic White Silk, Arancio Xanto, Giallo Belenus, Verde Scandal, Viola Pasifae and Blu Uranus. The last five colours come from Automobili Lamborghini's Ad Personam programme. Performance and Corse liveries are also available.

Factory-installed homologated options include Front Brake PRO and PRO+ packages, an STM dry clutch and adjustable footpegs. The programme is currently available in Europe and select international markets; its availability in India has not been confirmed.

data.title: Omaxe partners with Lemon Tree Hotels for 10 hotels with 4,000 keys
data.description:
Omaxe Ltd has entered into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Carnation Hotels Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Lemon Tree Hotels, to operate 10 hotel projects across India, comprising 4,000 keys. Announced on October 16, 2026, the arrangement marks a step in Omaxe’s Rs 6,200 crore hospitality expansion, unveiled in June 2026, which envisages 19 hotels across five states.

The 10 projects involve an estimated investment of Rs 4,000 crore and span Lucknow, Vrindavan, Amausi, Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Amritsar, Kaushambi and Faridabad. The portfolio covers transit hubs, pilgrimage destinations and commercial locations, with properties to be operated under Lemon Tree Hotels’ brand portfolio.

The projects will follow a sale-led development model, with Omaxe expecting to fund completion through sales proceeds without requiring loan funding. Development and commissioning timelines are expected to range from nine months to five years, depending on the project.

Mohit Goel, managing director, Omaxe, said, “India’s hospitality opportunity is expanding beyond established metropolitan markets, with Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities emerging as important destinations for business, leisure and pilgrimage travel. Temple towns, growing commercial centres and transit hubs each have distinct accommodation needs, creating an opportunity to develop hospitality assets that are aligned with the demand drivers of their respective markets. Our arrangement with Lemon Tree Hotels brings established operating expertise to this strategy, while our sale-led development model enables us to pursue this expansion with a disciplined approach to capital deployment.”

Neelendra Singh, managing director, Lemon Tree Hotels, said, “Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities have long been central to our India growth strategy, and this operating arrangement lets us scale it faster, from transit hubs in Lucknow to temple towns like Vrindavan. Omaxe brings nearly four decades of real estate development experience across these markets, while Lemon Tree brings over two decades of hospitality expertise and guest trust. This alliance combines developer scale with operating strength, and two trusted Indian brands with a proven record of execution, to build the next phase of growth. This will accelerate Lemon Tree Hotels’ asset-light growth strategy, enabling the Company to expand its managed portfolio across diverse markets and asset formats.”

The proposed portfolio includes two bus terminal developments in Lucknow, with 500 keys at Jankipuram and 330 keys at Vrindavan Yojna; a 693-key project at Omaxe BeTogether Centre Point, Amausi, near the airport; and two Vrindavan properties, Omaxe Eternity-II with 501 keys and Omaxe BeTogether Courtyard with 81 keys.

Other projects include Omaxe BeTogether Centre Point on Ambedkar Road in Ghaziabad (215 keys), Omaxe Connaught Place in Greater Noida (150 keys), service apartments in Amritsar (745 keys), Omaxe BeTogether Centre Point, Tower 1, in Kaushambi (350 keys), and World Mall in Sector 79, Faridabad (435 keys).

The arrangement extends Omaxe’s real estate development activities into hospitality, complementing its existing townships, commercial destinations and mixed-use developments.
